recognition.text: Ranked #6 on ESA/Hubble’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: This Hubble portrait shows NGC 2525, a barred spiral galaxy nearly 70 million light-years from Earth in the southern constellation Puppis. Together with Carina and Vela, Puppis makes up the image of the Argo, the ship from ancient Greek mythology.

A barred spiral has a straight band of stars across its centre, with the spiral arms reaching out from the ends. Like nearly every galaxy, NGC 2525 also hides a supermassive black hole at its core. Their masses can span from hundreds of thousands of Suns up to billions.

Hubble photographed this galaxy repeatedly for one of its major projects: measuring how fast the universe is expanding, which can help answer fundamental questions about its very nature. From those observations, ESA/Hubble produced a time-lapse showing the galaxy together with a supernova slowly fading inside it.
scale: NGC 2525 lies nearly 70 million light-years from Earth, according to ESA/Hubble.

understand.summary: Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3 observed this galaxy in visible and near-infrared light; the colour assigned to each filter isn't published.
understand.eye: Part of the data is near-infrared light, which is invisible to the human eye.
